System A:
  Clarity: 8.3/10
  Engagement: 7.6/10
  Depth Appropriateness: 8.5/10
  Breadth: 8.7/10
System B:
  Clarity: 8.1/10
  Engagement: 7.2/10
  Depth Appropriateness: 7.4/10
  Breadth: 7.8/10
System C:
  Clarity: 7.5/10
  Engagement: 6.4/10
  Depth Appropriateness: 6.8/10
  Breadth: 7.0/10

Explanation:
[A|Clarity] Round 1 overview explains the PV/PVC/StorageClass triad with a concrete mechanism ("A PersistentVolume (PV) is the actual piece of storage... A PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is a user's request") and the lifecycle runs are traced step-by-step; Round 2's instructor answer on snapshots vs file-level backup states the trade-off plainly ("capture is near-instant and restore is a fast clone... The price is speed"). Minor gaps: some CSI driver internals and CMEK/egress details are named without full unpacking, keeping it just below the top anchor.

[A|Engagement] The student's selected questions track the user's stated intent (e.g., Round 1's snapshots-vs-file-level trade-off question directly serves "necessity of persistent storage and backup"), and each instructor answer closes with a practical takeaway ("build a layered plan... then prove it works with scheduled restore drills"). Engagement is purposeful but the user never issues mid-process guidance, so involvement is largely inferred from question selection rather than demonstrated user participation.

[A|Depth Appropriateness] Foundations (PV/PVC/reclaim policy) are established in Round 1 before Round 2-3 develop cross-cloud data movement, quiescing mechanisms, and etcd-only restore assumptions — a coherent progression matching the "introduction" intent while adding conditional detail ("the destination cluster needs a CSI driver that can actually provision the restored volume"). Uncertainties are flagged ("verify against your driver and tool docs"), which serves depth appropriately.

[A|Breadth] Four distinct dimensions are developed and connected: storage lifecycle, backup tooling (snapshots vs file-level vs data movement), DR/RPO-RTO planning, and consistency/security — with explicit relationships ("these are complementary, not competing"). The final summary consolidates all four areas. Some security/retention material in the overview is only lightly developed relative to the storage and backup threads.

[B|Clarity] Round 1 and Round 2 answers explain PV/PVC/StorageClass and the three backup layers with clear reasoning ("Backing up only one layer is insufficient: restoring manifests without volume data gives you a working cluster with empty databases"). The Round 3 answer organizes eleven follow-on topics, though several (RBAC, compliance, GitOps) receive one-paragraph treatments that name rather than fully explain.

[B|Engagement] Responses consistently tie back to the user's intent ("why do Kubernetes users actually need persistent storage and backup? Because stateful workloads... need their data to outlive the pod"), and Round 3's "What else should I know" is answered with a structured checklist. However, the process is essentially three independent Q&A turns with no user follow-up shaping direction, so sustained involvement is limited.

[B|Depth Appropriateness] Round 1-2 give workable introductory depth (access modes, reclaim policy, Velero's role), but Round 3's breadth-first list ("1. Reframe... 11. Adapt for managed Kubernetes") trades mechanism for enumeration — several items (compliance, RBAC, cost) are named with generic function rather than explained conditions or trade-offs. Depth is adequate for an introduction but flattens in the final round.

[B|Breadth] The three-layer backup model, Velero's use cases, consistency levels, CSI snapshots, restore difficulties, RPO/RTO, security, GitOps, and managed-Kubernetes specifics form a well-connected set of perspectives relevant to the stated intent. The relationships (e.g., "GitOps and backups are complementary, not redundant") are stated, though some Round 3 items are checklist entries rather than developed dimensions.

[C|Clarity] The warm-start and Round 1-2 answers explain binding mechanics clearly ("A control loop in the master watches for new PVCs, finds a matching PV... binds them together"), and the final summary's StorageClass section traces reclaim policy, binding mode, and expansion with reasons. However, Round 1's answer is heavily AKS/Azure-Backup-specific without framing why that scope was chosen, and Round 3's platform-engineer turn explicitly flags missing coverage ("the gathered material doesn't cover StorageClass provisioning mechanics, reclaim policies... so I can't back those points"), leaving a visible gap the user must reconcile.

[C|Engagement] The warm-start dialogue poses pointed moderator questions ("where do teams most often trip up?") that create a discussion-like entry, and Round 2 directly addresses the user's educational intent. But Round 1's answer narrows to Azure Backup specifics without user prompting, and Round 3 is an autonomous continuation ("No new user input") in which the speaker itself notes evidence limits — involvement becomes passive delivery rather than supported participation.

[C|Depth Appropriateness] Foundations in PV/PVC binding are explained at introductory depth, and the final summary's StorageClass and snapshot-scheduling sections add mechanism (DeletionPolicy, ListSnapshots, WaitForFirstConsumer). However, Round 1's Azure Backup policy details (retention priority ordering, vault tiers) are operational specifics that exceed an "introduction" framing, while Round 3's platform-engineer turn under-delivers on reclaim policies and ephemeral storage by its own admission — an uneven depth profile.

[C|Breadth] The record spans PV/PVC binding, dynamic provisioning, StorageClass parameters, snapshot prerequisites, cross-cluster portability, and Velero's CSI integration — a reasonable multidimensional set. The warm-start adds reclaim-policy and binding-mode traps. However, backup-side coverage is thinner than storage-side (etcd, RPO/RTO, restore testing appear only lightly), and Round 1's Azure-specific policy material narrows rather than broadens the general Kubernetes picture.
